title: Q: Hydrogen and oxygen react separately to give H₂O₂ and H₂O — what law of stoichiometry is illustrated?
notes: Two elements (hydrogen and oxygen) combine to form more than one compound: H₂O and H₂O₂
For a fixed mass of hydrogen (2 g), the masses of oxygen that combine are 16 g (in H₂O) and 32 g (in H₂O₂)
Ratio of oxygen masses = 16 : 32 = **1 : 2** — a simple whole-number ratio
**Answer: this illustrates the Law of Multiple Proportions**
